title: Your body is a temple (1 Corinthians 6:12–20)
hook: you are not your own; you were bought with a price
tomorrow: the Corinthians mailed Paul their questions. what did they ask?

segments.voice: Yesterday, fools for Christ, answering insult with blessing. The line: being reviled, we bless.

"It's my body, my call." People say it about sleep, food, screens, all of it. Corinth had a slogan like that: "All things are lawful unto me". Some readers think it was a saying going round the church. Paul doesn't throw it out. He finishes it: "but all things are not expedient". Not everything helps. Then again: "but I will not be brought under the power of any." Free, yes. Owned by nothing, also yes.
screen: `MY BODY, MY CALL.` → `ALL THINGS ARE LAWFUL.` → `BUT NOT ALL THINGS HELP.`

segments.voice: Some readers hear a second slogan right after: "Meats for the belly, and the belly for meats". The body as a machine: what you do with it never touches the soul. Paul disagrees: "the body is not for fornication, but for the Lord; and the Lord for the body." The Lord is for the body. That's the surprise. Then today's line: "What? know ye not that your body is the temple of the Holy Ghost which is in you, which ye have of God, and ye are not your own?" Two days ago the temple was all of you together. Now it comes closer. "For ye are bought with a price: therefore glorify God in your body, and in your spirit, which are God's." So the body isn't a shell or a trophy. It's a place where God lives, and it was paid for. For Paul, in this chapter, that means sexual faithfulness. Some Christians draw more from the line too: rest, food, care, and respect for other people's bodies as well as their own.
screen: `NOT ALL THINGS HELP.` · `THE LORD FOR THE BODY.` · `A TEMPLE OF THE HOLY GHOST.` · `BOUGHT WITH A PRICE.` · then, large: `GLORIFY GOD IN YOUR BODY.`

segments.voice: Close your eyes and move your attention slowly through your body: feet, hands, shoulders, breath, grading none of it. Where you find tiredness, rest there kindly, the way you'd tend a room where someone you love lives.
Your body is a temple. Paul's answer to a church that said the body didn't matter: it does, because God lives there.
screen: `YOUR BODY IS A TEMPLE — today's word`.

segments.voice: Your line: glorify God in your body. It was bought with a price, tired as it is. Rest well.

chat.meaning: Paul says the body is a temple, not a machine to run down. Some Christians read that as care too: sleep, food, rest.
